# SecureChat – full description

> SecureChat (https://securechat.online/) is a free, open-source web app for anonymous one-to-one text and video chat with a random stranger. No account, no sign-up, no chat history. Text is end-to-end encrypted between the two browsers.

## What it is

SecureChat pairs two people at random for a text chat or a video chat, straight in the browser. Nobody is asked for a name, email address or phone number. When a chat ends, it is gone: there is no database and no message history.

## How to use it

1. Open https://securechat.online/.
2. Confirm you are 18 or older and accept the rules (shown once, remembered on your device, and withdrawable from "Rules and privacy").
3. Choose "Start text chat" or "Start video chat". Camera and microphone access is only requested for video.
4. Chat. Use "Next" to move on to someone else, "Report" if someone breaks the rules, or the hide-now button (Alt+X) to leave and hide the chat instantly.

Optional: add up to five interests and a language under "Match preferences". People who share them are matched first; after a few seconds anyone will do. "Create invite link" or a room code puts you in a private room that only people with the code can join.

## Features

- Text chat with formatting, emoji, reactions, replies, read receipts, typing indicator and photo sharing (photos are compressed and encrypted in the browser, and hidden on the receiving side until shown).
- Peer-to-peer video over WebRTC with mute, camera off, device pickers, screen share, picture-in-picture and full screen. A text chat can be upgraded to video if both people agree.
- Safety tools: report, next, leave, hide-now panic button, neutral tab title, strong-language filter, link warnings, optional blurring of the partner's video.
- Light and dark themes, keyboard shortcuts (press ? in the app), screen-reader labels, reduced-motion support.
- Installable as a progressive web app with an offline shell.

## Privacy and security model

- Text: the two browsers agree a key with ECDH (P-256) using the Web Crypto API and encrypt every message with AES-256-GCM. Sending is disabled until the key exists. Reactions, replies, photos and receipts travel inside the same encrypted envelope.
- Key exchange is relayed, so a safety code is shown in the lock menu. If both people see the same code, nobody is in the middle.
- Video and audio are encrypted by WebRTC (DTLS-SRTP) and flow directly between browsers. In a video call, each browser learns the other's IP address. Use a VPN if that matters.
- Anything shown or said can be recorded by the other person. There are no moderators.
- On the public site, matchmaking and call setup run serverless over public MQTT brokers; only encrypted text and connection setup messages pass through them.
- The optional self-hosted Node.js server relays messages and call setup, keeps no database, and logs only short operational lines.
- The page runs under a strict Content Security Policy and loads no third-party scripts, fonts or trackers.

## Rules

Treat people the way you want to be treated. No harassment, hate, sexual content involving minors, threats, spam or illegal activity. Users must be 18 or older.

## FAQ

**Is SecureChat free?** Yes. There is no paid tier and no ads.

**Do I need an account?** No. There is nothing to sign up for.

**Are chats saved?** No. Messages exist only in the two browsers for the length of the chat.

**Can the server read my messages?** Text messages are encrypted before they leave your browser, so the relay only sees scrambled text. Compare the safety code with your partner to be sure.

**Does it work on phones?** Yes, in any modern mobile browser. Video needs camera permission and a secure (HTTPS) connection.

**Can I chat with a friend instead of a stranger?** Yes. Create an invite link or share a room code from "Match preferences and private rooms".

**Can I host my own copy?** Yes. The source is MIT-licensed at https://github.com/0x0806/securechat and runs on any static host or with the included Node.js server.
